_: The update card's changelog. Newest first. Each entry: build (the stamp it shipped as), title, notes. newsSince() shows entries until it meets the running build — keep this list short and honest.

entries.title: A lava lamp that is simulated, not animated
notes: a new room — THE LAVA LAMP: wax that rises because it is warm, thins because it is hot, tears apart when it is going too fast, and rings like a struck drop for a second after two blobs collapse into one

the pool at the bottom is stuck to the heater by its own wetting film and pays out droplets from underneath — and on the rare occasion it warms enough to let go, it comes apart into a rising column of droplets on the way up, which nobody scripted

real refraction through the surface, split into three wavelengths, over the coil’s own light in the fluid behind; thin edges pale, fat middles deep, and bubbles that zig-zag on the way up the way rising bubbles actually do
the music is the thermostat: bass and the track’s arc turn the coil up, and everything else — how fast the wax climbs, how readily it breaks — follows from that one number
put a hand on it and the wax flows, and keeps flowing after you let go
a device that cannot afford as many blobs gets fewer, larger ones rather than a coarser picture — which is more like a lava lamp, not less

entries.title: The field can have a screen of its own
notes: stage mode: the visualizer goes fullscreen on a second screen or a TV and this window becomes the booth — hold the fullscreen button, press ⇧F, or tap Stage
the booth folds into a corner player: what is playing, the transport, and a pad that puts your hand on the picture the room can see — the chevron opens the rest
a stage screen carries no controls, no library and no sound of its own; it draws what the booth hears, and says so if the booth goes quiet instead of freezing
several screens draw one field rather than one picture each — screen 2 of 3 shows the middle third of a single camera, so a shape crossing the seam stays one shape
fixed: on the Mac app, CATALOG opened nothing and stalled the audio — every dialog is the app’s own now, so naming a journey and erasing history work there too
the microphone says which of the four things went wrong, and on the Mac it opens the privacy pane where the answer actually lives
the Mac app no longer offers to install the app you are already in
the Mac app’s own update is offered instead of installed behind your back — same card, same three choices, and your place is saved before it restarts

entries.title: "You're up to date" — a status that finally says so
notes: fixed: the update card could still come back reading "→ new" over and over — an announcement from an outdated background worker, or a check made while the site was unreachable, was believed without ever being verified
an offer that cannot name the build it brings is now re-checked against the site on every update check, and withdrawn the moment it turns out to be the build you already run

when a check finds you current while the card is open, the card now says "You're up to date" with the build id — and applying a refresh says the same, so the end of the loop is something you can actually see

entries.title: The update that knew it had landed
notes: fixed: applying an update could leave the app offering you the same one again, over and over, with nothing left to apply — an update you have already applied is now recognised as applied, and the app says so once instead of asking again
the check for a newer version asks the site itself rather than the copy it already has, so "there is an update" is something measured and not something assumed
a background update that carries the version you are running is retired quietly instead of becoming a card — and when there really is a new one, the card names it instead of calling it "new"
the what's-new list is the news you do not have yet: builds that shipped without a note of their own no longer make it repeat the last four

entries.title: The booth grew hands
notes: loops and rolls on eight beat lengths, from a 32nd to sixteen bars — a loop makes the track wait, a roll stalls the music while the track runs on underneath, so letting go lands you where you would have been
a loop latches on the last beat line you actually heard, and halving or doubling it never moves where it began
filter, echo, gate and drive on one knob, every time constant read from the same beat clock the visuals follow — plus a brake that is a turntable losing power, not a fade
AUTO gives the same hands to the room: the echo blooms into a hand-off and the filter opens across a build, chosen from the song's own shape and never during a quiet passage
the moment you touch anything, AUTO steps back and stays back until you arm it again — it will not undo what you just set
fixed: the gate could silently stop on a busy frame instead of chopping
fixed: the booth could knock a blend off its beat lock by resetting a deck's speed just as the mix began

entries.title: The update that kept asking
notes: fixed: the app could offer you an update to the version you were already running, and keep offering it after you applied it
an update is only offered now when the build on the server is genuinely different from the one you have
when a check turns out to be a false alarm, the badge clears itself instead of waiting for a reload

entries.title: No more silence between tracks on iPhone
notes: the next track is now fetched while the current one plays, so the hand-off no longer waits on the network — the gap on a phone drops from over two seconds to the time the player itself needs
this works with the lock screen, not around it: playback never leaves the one element iOS trusts with background audio
on a slow or metered connection the app leaves it alone — Data Saver and 2G/3G are respected
touching the visuals now works on every device: weaker phones get a simpler version of the effect instead of none at all

entries.title: Your hand bends the world now
notes: the touch no longer draws anything on top of the visuals — it deforms the space they live in, and everything obeys
the black hole is genuinely dark because light near it stops coming back, and the bright ring around it is real lensing
hold your finger down and the horizon widens; let go and a wavefront leaves your fingertip and travels out
scenes with no particles answer your touch for the first time — the light itself is bent, so every scene reacts
reduced motion keeps the touch alive at a gentler strength instead of switching it off

entries.title: The auto-mix holds its beat lock
notes: the intermittent glitch in the auto mix is fixed — blends stayed in time on an idle machine and drifted up to a quarter beat when the visuals were working hard
the seam is now lined up against where the outgoing track actually is, so a busy frame can no longer cost a blend its timing
the incoming track is given a moment to get rolling before the fader opens, so a blend starts full instead of easing in from nothing
measured under full visual load: beat error down from 114 ms to under 8 ms, and it is now a test that has to keep passing

entries.title: Shorter, tighter blends
notes: auto-mix now blends in 8 beats by default instead of 32 — a punchier mix, and far less room for two decks to drift apart
the crate's match scores now rate the PAIR (key and tempo) rather than rewarding whichever blend was longest
longer blends are still there per pair in the Mix tuner

entries.title: The Update button, fixed — and a log of what the app does
notes: tapping Update always does something now: if another window already applied it, this one reloads instead of going quiet
"Later" is remembered across restarts — the button keeps a count and reminds you once when the time is up
SHOW mode still holds every update; nothing is ever applied out from under a set
new Activity log at the bottom of the Console: updates, what played, what the system decided — kept on this device only

entries.title: Colour that survives the brightest moment
notes: bright scenes no longer wash out to white — overdriven light reads as deeper colour instead
blowing out to white is saved for the drop, where the music has earned it
the palette is now a full gradient, so sweeps stay vivid instead of going grey in the middle
click the three colour dots in the HUD: AUTO · SPECTRUM · DUOTONE

entries.title: Four more skins
notes: Sakura Night, Solstice, Ultramarine, Garnet & Silver — 12 in all
dialogs, the update bar, and the welcome card now follow your skin too

entries.title: Skins + a bulletproof update bar
notes: 8 skins — dress the whole console; your pick stays on this device
the welcome says it plainly: a free jukebox, loaded and ready
updating shows an honest progress bar that never gets stuck
if a swap ever stalls, the player hands itself back — nothing lost

entries.title: Smart self-updating
notes: updates now arrive by themselves — no more clearing site data
the Update button wears a badge and opens this log
choose: now, after this track, or later (6 h)
⚡ SHOW mode is never interrupted by an update

entries.title: The epic touch
notes: hold to charge, release to detonate
sling the vortex and it keeps spinning
tap on the beat — the field answers louder
✦ AUTO: scenes re-tune your touch as they change

entries.title: Echoes — passing thoughts
notes: quotes drift by like clouds in the calm passages
✧ MUSE floats questions you can answer, kept on this device only

entries.title: Power modes
notes: ⚡ SHOW: full density, screen kept awake
⚡ ECO: half the frames, quarter the pixels — battery goes to the music

entries.title: Mobile booth redesign
notes: real platters on mobile, a live monitor between them
